title: Contract Change Financial Impact Playbook
author: Jordan Liao
body:
Overview
=======

Purpose: This playbook describes the cross-functional procedure for assessing the financial impact of contract changes (amendments, addenda, credits, term extensions, early terminations, SOW changes) and operationalizing updates into the budget, forecast, procurement system, and revenue recognition. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Sales Operations, Procurement and Revenue Operations.

Scope: Applies to all customer and vendor contract changes that: (a) alter committed revenue/expense by >= $25,000 annualized, or (b) change billing timing by more than 30 days, or (c) modify contract term by > 90 days. Lower-value changes may follow an abbreviated path in Section: "Quick Path".

Principles
----------
- Single source of truth: Contract system (DocuSign/CLM) + Billing system (Stripe/Zuora) + Forecast (Adaptive/Anaplan) must be consistent.
- Fast, auditable decisions: Target review SLA is 5 business days for standard amendments, 10 business days for complex amendments.
- Clear ownership: Each amendment must have a named Financial Reviewer and Legal Reviewer recorded in the contract record.
- RevRec-first mindset: Changes are evaluated with ASC 606 (or local GAAP equivalent) impact as the gating criterion for recognition and deferral treatment.

Key Stakeholders and Roles
--------------------------
- Requesting Team (Sales/Procurement) — owns business justification and customer communication.
- Legal — validates contractual language and signs the amendment.
- Finance (RevRec) — determines revenue recognition impact and accounting treatment.
- FP&A — updates forecast and budget, communicates variance to owners.
- Billing/Revenue Ops — updates billing system, issues credits/invoices, and ensures collections mapping.
- Procurement (vendor-side changes) — mirrors process for cost-side impact.

Definitions
-----------
- Amendment: any signed document that changes price/term/delivery of an existing contract.
- Material Change: change meeting scope thresholds in Scope section.
- Billing Trigger: the event that drives invoice issuance (e.g., effective date, milestone completion).

Decision Matrix (text table)
---------------------------
This table should be reproduced in the contract record as a checklist.

| Change Type | Material Threshold | Accounting Gate | Primary Reviewer | SLA |
|------------|--------------------|-----------------|------------------|-----|
| Price increase / decrease | >= $25k ARR | Assess for contract modification under ASC 606; remeasurement or cumulative catch-up | Finance (RevRec) | 5 biz days |
| Term extension / contraction | > 90 days | Evaluate effect on performance obligations and timing of recognition | Finance (RevRec) | 7 biz days |
| Billing schedule change (defer/accelerate) | Any change > 30 days | Determine whether contract consideration remains the same and if modification leads to variable consideration | Finance + Billing Ops | 5 biz days |
| Credit / refund request | Any | Assess whether credit is a separate transaction or reduces consideration | Finance + Legal | 5 biz days |
| SOW / deliverable re-scope | Any | Determine whether scope change creates new distinct performance obligations | Finance + PM | 10 biz days |

Procedure: Contract Change Review (detailed)
-------------------------------------------
1. Intake and triage (Requesting Team)
   - Create amendment record in CLM within 1 business day, attach redline and business rationale.
   - Tag the record with estimated financial impact (must be a number or range).
   - Assign primary Financial Reviewer (FP&A or RevRec) and Legal Reviewer in the CLM.

2. Legal review (Legal)
   - Confirm amendment language is executable and capture effective date, termination provisions, and any warranty/penalty clauses.
   - If new terms change risk profile, escalate to Security/Compliance.

3. Accounting impact analysis (Finance — RevRec)
   - Within SLA, run a modification assessment aligned to ASC 606 checklist:
     a. Is there a separate distinct good/service?
     b. Does the change add a distinct price that reflects standalone selling price?
     c. Does performance obligation period change?
   - Outcome: (i) No change to recognized revenue (operational update only), (ii) Prospective treatment (future billing adjusted), (iii) Cumulative catch-up (unless contract scope indicates otherwise).
   - Document: accounting memo (one paragraph) and store in CLM record.

4. Forecast and budget update (FP&A)
   - If material, update the rolling forecast and mark variance reason code: "Contract Amendment".
   - Recalculate ARR / TCV impact and update pipeline/commit numbers.
   - Communicate changes to Sales leadership and Customer Success if renewal/health is impacted.

5. Billing system execution (Billing/Revenue Ops)
   - Translate amendment into billing instructions: invoice schedule, credit memos, proration rules.
   - Implement credits or invoices only after Finance memo sign-off.
   - For refunds/credits > $10k, require Treasury approval for cash impact.

6. Procurement (vendor-side changes)
   - Mirror the steps above for supplier contract changes.
   - Ensure PO amendments are issued before accepting changed supplier on new terms.

7. Close and audit trail
   - Mark record as "Complete" in CLM and attach all artifacts (signed amendment, accounting memo, billing ticket, forecast update).
   - Update monthly contract-change register owned by Finance Ops.

Quick Path: Low-value changes (< $25k ARR and no timing change)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- Sales/Procurement may route to an expedited review: Legal notification + Billing Ops update with a single-step Finance acknowledgement email. Target SLA: 2 business days.

Templates and Examples
---------------------
- Accounting memo template (one-paragraph): "Contract ABC amendment increases monthly fee from $X to $Y effective DATE. Assessment: There is no new distinct performance obligation; the amendment is a contract modification accounted for prospectively; deferred revenue change = $Z. Reviewer: NAME, DATE."

- Billing instruction example (free text to Billing Ops):
  "Apply prorated credit of $2,400 on invoice 2026-001 for period 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30. Issue one-time invoice of $12,000 on 2026-05-01 for new service. Reference contract: C-2026-589."

Accounting and RevRec Notes (practical rules)
---------------------------------------------
- Use the following fast checks: if price change is for a distinct add-on with standalone price -> treat as separate contract; if the change modifies remaining promised goods/services -> treat as contract modification.
- For term > 12 months additions that include discounts, compute implicit rate and compare to historical ARR to determine variable consideration constraints.
- All cumulative catch-ups must be approved by Accounting Manager and recorded in the close period following sign-off.

Systems and Tags
----------------
- CLM: DocuSign + ContractWorkbench (contract-id). Required fields on amendment record: financial-impact-estimate, finance-reviewer, legal-reviewer, revrec-treatment, billing-ticket-id.
- Forecast system: Tag change with variance code "CONTRACT_AMENDMENT" and include CLM id.
- Billing system: All credits must reference both invoice-id and CLM-id.

SLAs and Escalation Path
------------------------
- Standard escalation: 48 hours after SLA breach -> Finance Manager; 72 hours -> Head of Finance; 5 business days -> CFO notification for enterprise accounts.

Audit Controls and Evidence
---------------------------
- Required artifacts for audit: signed amendment, accounting memo, updated invoice(s) or credit memos, FP&A forecast snapshot before/after, email approvals when applicable.
- Retain artifacts for minimum 7 years per company retention policy.

Operational metrics to track
--------------------------
- Median time to close amendment (target: <= 5 business days).
- % of amendments triggering cumulative catch-up.
- Number of forecast adjustments attributable to contract changes (monthly).
- Billing exceptions created per quarter.

Appendix: Checklist (to paste into CLM record)
---------------------------------------------
1. Amendment uploaded to CLM with business rationale.
2. Financial estimate entered.
3. Legal and Finance reviewers assigned.
4. Accounting memo attached.
5. Billing ticket created and linked.
6. Forecast updated (if material).
7. Signed amendment stored and record closed.
